issue.title: just check fails at lint (symvision): 10 unused public glossary/memory-web symbols, masked until the chat_fork private-import errors were fixed
issue.description:
`just check` fails at lint (symvision) on master `2d908ca11` with 10 unused public
symbols in the glossary / memory-web surface:

```
GlossaryReadAgentSummary        in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
GlossaryReadError               in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
GlossaryReadTermSummary         in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
summarize_glossary_reads_by_agent in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
summarize_glossary_reads_by_term  in src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py
build_relation_chip_rows        in src/sase/ace/tui/modals/glossary_preview_render.py
filter_glossary_entries         in src/sase/memory/web/text_filter.py
fsync_directory                 in src/sase/memory/atomic_write.py
render_glossary_catalog         in src/sase/memory/web/render.py
render_glossary_closure         in src/sase/memory/web/render.py
```

## Why this only appears now

These findings were **masked**, not new. Symvision reports one error class and exits,
and on clean master the private-import class (task `sase-tb`, the split
`src/sase/history/chat_fork/` submodules) fired first. `sase-t8.land` fixed `sase-tb`
by promoting those cross-module helpers to public names; symvision then advanced to the
next class and surfaced these 10. Reproduced both ways on the same tree:

- clean master (`git stash`): only the 18 `chat_fork` private-import errors.
- with the `chat_fork` fix applied: only these 10 unused-public errors.

So this is a *pre-existing* red gate on master, independent of epic `sase-t8`, whose
only relationship to it is ordering inside symvision's output.

## Cause

Every symbol belongs to the memory-web / glossary-migration work landed by epic
`sase-sq` ("Memory webs and strands", closed 2026-08-25T08:15:17Z) — in particular the
`sase-sq.7`/`sase-sq.8` glossary migration and config-glossary retirement. Each symbol
has **no non-test consumer**; the only references outside its own defining module are
in `tests/`, which per `sase/memory/symvision.md` never keeps a public symbol alive:

- `tests/test_glossary_read_log.py` for `GlossaryReadError`,
  `summarize_glossary_reads_by_agent`, `summarize_glossary_reads_by_term`
- `tests/ace/tui/modals/test_glossary_preview_render.py` for `build_relation_chip_rows`
- `GlossaryReadAgentSummary`, `GlossaryReadTermSummary`, `filter_glossary_entries`,
  `fsync_directory`, `render_glossary_catalog`, `render_glossary_closure` have no
  reference at all outside their own file.

`src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py` looks entirely dead — five of the ten
symbols live there.

## Remediation

Work the `sase/memory/symvision.md` hierarchy per symbol, not uniformly: delete
genuinely dead code (and its tests), privatize what is used only inside its own file,
and use a non-test pragma only where a real consumer exists that symvision cannot see.
Deciding whether `legacy_glossary_read_log.py` is a deliberate compatibility shim (kept
for a follow-up) or plain dead code from the retirement is the judgment call this task
exists to make — `sase-t8.land` deliberately did not guess at it while landing an
unrelated epic.

Verify with `just _lint-symvision` and then `just check`.

## Discovery

Found by `sase-t8.land` while landing epic `sase-t8` ("Fork every SASE shell"). NOT
caused by that epic: `sase-t8`'s three commits (`4fb8f3bae`, `2a3e1d2c6`, `69dc50a31`)
touch fork/wait/ACE code and never `src/sase/memory/**` or the glossary modal.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic static lint failure, not a timing-dependent test. Symvision scans src/sase/ and reports these 10 symbols on every run against an unchanged tree; reproduced repeatedly at master 2d908ca11, and reproduced under git stash to prove the findings are pre-existing rather than introduced by the working-tree diff.
